extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff, and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria governing approval of an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. §11.27 and the resulting exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO, including the misconduct rules alleged, publication/redaction requirements, and reinstatement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. §11.27
rubrics_metrics.description: An Affidavit of Resignation pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.27 is submitted by a practitioner for approval by the USPTO Director for the purpose of being excluded on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director determines whether the affidavit complies with §11.27(a); if approved, the practitioner is excluded on consent from practice in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary, knowing consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner's consent to exclusion must be freely and voluntarily rendered and not obtained by coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should expressly acknowledge that the practitioner's consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and that the practitioner understands the legal consequences of consenting to exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of OED investigation and allegations (per 37 C.F.R. §11.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must be aware that the OED Director opened an investigation of allegations and must acknowledge the existence/nature of those investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit typically references OED file numbers and summarizes the types of information obtained in the investigations (e.g., facts about particular patent or trademark matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of potential findings and effects on reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: By consenting to exclusion, the practitioner acknowledges that the OED Director is of the opinion certain misconduct occurred and that upon any future reinstatement application the OED Director will presume the allegations true for reinstatement purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit may state that, if and when the practitioner applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. §11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume the allegations are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended against them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to inform a client of important correspondence (37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violative conduct includes failing to inform a client of important correspondence received from the USPTO, such as Office Actions, Notices of Abandonment, or Notices of Allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the record: practitioner received Office Actions and Notices of Abandonment/Allowance but did not notify clients nor file responsive papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing a paper filed in the Office in violation of §11.18 (37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(15))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing or signing papers in the USPTO in a manner that violates §11.18 (e.g., signature requirements) is misconduct under the Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office considered conduct falling within this provision when filings were made improperly or without proper authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(4); §11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation to clients or the Office is a basis for disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative misconduct: making misleading statements to clients about application status, fabricating documents purporting to come from the USPTO, and certifying untruthfully that delays were unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice is proscribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is applied where behavior undermines fair and proper functioning of USPTO processes (e.g., false certifications that affect granting of petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowingly giving false or misleading information to a client or to the Office (37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(2)(i) & (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly providing false or misleading information to a client in connection with business before the Office, or to the Office or its employees, is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case examples include falsely stating an application was pending or that a Track 1 filing had been made and providing fabricated status documents to a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting a legal matter entrusted to a practitioner (37 C.F.R. §10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglect of a legal matter entrusted to a practitioner (e.g., failure to respond to Office Actions, failure to file or revive applications) constitutes grounds for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: not filing responses to Office Actions, allowing applications to become abandoned without client knowledge, not taking action to revive abandoned matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to seek lawful objectives, carry out contract of employment, or prejudicing/damaging a client (37 C.F.R. §10.84(a)(1),(2),(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to pursue a client's lawful objectives, failing to carry out contractual employment obligations, or prejudicing/damaging a client are disciplinary violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner's omissions or misrepresentations resulted in client harm (e.g., loss of patent prosecution rights and client injury).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to represent a client with reasonable competence (37 C.F.R. §11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the post-May 3, 2013 Rules of Professional Conduct, a practitioner must represent a client with a reasonable degree of competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include inadequate prosecution practices, failure to respond to USPTO communications, and other lapses that undermine competent representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to reasonably communicate with a client (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(2) & (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must reasonably communicate with clients about the status of matters and important developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record cites numerous instances where the practitioner failed to inform clients of Office Actions, Notices of Abandonment/Allowance, or the actual filing status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicing law in violation of jurisdictional regulation (37 C.F.R. §11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practicing law in a jurisdiction in a manner that violates that jurisdiction's regulation of the legal profession (including practice while administratively suspended) is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: practitioner continued to practice before the USPTO after administrative suspension for failure to respond to the mandatory survey, including filing new applications and failing to withdraw from pending matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of administrative suspension for failure to respond to practitioner survey (37 C.F.R. §11.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to respond to mandatory practitioner survey can result in administrative suspension under §11.11(b), which bars practice before the USPTO until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must monitor and respond to survey/noncompliance notices; continuing to practice while administratively suspended constitutes additional misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for Director to approve exclusion (35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) & 32; 37 C.F.R. §11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO has statutory and regulatory authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions taken pursuant to these statutes/regulations result in issuance of a Final Order effecting exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and redaction requirements for Final Orders and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette; certain information must be redacted from the publicly posted Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically required redactions include (1) OED file numbers referenced in specified paragraphs, (2) client names and application numbers referenced in particular paragraphs, and (3) names of clients and application numbers referenced in the Notice of Exclusion on Consent. The Official Gazette notice must be 'materially consistent' with the prescribed text (with redactions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 (effect of exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner excluded on consent must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 concerning the effect of exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 covers obligations such as ceasing practice before the USPTO and handling client files/notifications as required by the rules (affidavit here explicitly orders compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.60 upon any request for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the excluded practitioner seeks reinstatement, the practitioner must comply fully with the procedures and requirements of 37 C.F.R. §11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit and Final Order note that reinstatement applications will be evaluated under §11.60 and that the OED Director will apply the presumption described above for reinstatement considerations.
